summary: Biogen/Ionis tau drug diranersen was the meeting's headline, slowing decline 38% at two years, though the comparison is imperfect.
Five-year and real-world Leqembi data support durability and lower real-world brain-swelling rates, but against external, not placebo, controls.
BMS gave a first look at Cobenfy in Alzheimer's psychosis, open-label only; placebo-controlled pivotal readouts arrive in 2027.
Misses outnumbered wins: Acadia, Lilly mevidalen, Cognito and Priavoid fell short; AriBio's oral AR1001 succeeded only in a subgroup.

items.title: CELIA Phase 2 two-year data, diranersen tau antisense drug (Biogen; Ionis)
lines: Week 96: 60 mg twice-yearly slowed CDR-SB (Clinical Dementia Rating-Sum of Boxes) decline 38%, 1.09 points; n=60 vs 115 originally on placebo; p-value not reported.
Effect widened from 26% at week 76; ADAS-Cog13 (Alzheimer's Disease Assessment Scale-Cognitive, 13-item) slowing 54% at week 96.
Missed primary dose-response endpoint in May 2026; higher doses did worse; BMO Capital Markets called the control comparison imperfect.
Confusional states 14.8% on 60 mg vs 13.1% at July cut; spinal (intrathecal) dosing; no amyloid-related brain swelling; Phase 3 planned.

items.title: Clarity AD five-year extension and LEADER real-world study, Leqembi lecanemab (Eisai; Biogen)
lines: Five years: CDR-SB difference -2.05 points vs ADNI (Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative) and -2.54 vs BioFINDER observational cohorts; no confidence interval reported.
36% lower relative risk of progressing to next disease stage vs ADNI; only 351 of 1,795 enrolled had five continuous years.
ARIA-E (amyloid-related imaging abnormalities-edema) 13.5% in year one, below 1.5% per year afterwards; no new safety findings.
LEADER, n=560 at 13 US sites: 76% lower progression to moderate/severe dementia vs ADNI-weighted controls; ARIA-E 6.6%; 87.5% still treated.

items.title: ADEPT-1 and ADEPT-3 Phase 3 in Alzheimer's psychosis, Cobenfy (KarXT, xanomeline-trospium) (Bristol Myers Squibb)
lines: ADEPT-1 12-week open-label, 273 completers: NPI-C H+D (Neuropsychiatric Inventory-Clinician Hallucinations and Delusions) -12.0 points; CGI-S (Clinical Global Impression-Severity) -1.9; uncontrolled.
ADEPT-1 safety: treatment-emergent adverse events 56.6%, serious 5%, discontinuation for adverse events 4.4%.
ADEPT-3 52-week extension, 401 enrolled: NPI-C H+D -5.1, CGI-S -0.8; adverse events 65%, serious 7.7%, discontinuation 4.7%.
Randomized relapse endpoint not reported; placebo-controlled readouts 2027; Cobenfy sales $176 million in first nine months of 2026.

items.title: POLARIS-AD Phase 3, AR1001 oral PDE5 (phosphodiesterase-5) inhibitor (AriBio, private; Fosun Pharma statement)
lines: n=1,535 early Alzheimer's patients randomized to once-daily AR1001 or placebo for 52 weeks.
Prespecified monotherapy group n=604: CDR-SB slowing 0.44 points (31% per AriBio), primary objective met; p-value figures not reported.
Full population including cholinesterase inhibitor or memantine users: 0.11-point difference, not significant; MMSE (Mini-Mental State Examination) nominal +0.7 points in monotherapy group.
No amyloid-related brain swelling; discontinuation for adverse events 5.2% vs 1.7% placebo; AriBio plans FDA discussion.

items.title: Misses: remlifanserin (Acadia), mevidalen (Eli Lilly), Spectris device (Cognito, private), PRI-002 (Priavoid, private)
lines: Acadia RADIANT Phase 2 in Alzheimer's psychosis narrowly missed primary endpoint; 60 mg advancing to Phase 3, 30 mg dropped; figures not reported.
Lilly mevidalen PRESENCE-ALZ Phase 2, n=304: missed primary endpoint; no further development planned; effect figures not reported.
Cognito Spectris HOPE pivotal, n=673: missed primary and all overall secondary endpoints; mild subgroup favored on 5 of 5 measures, nominal only.
Priavoid PRImus-AD Phase 2, n=304: missed week-48 CDR-SB primary; ADAS-Cog13 slowing 35.9% per-protocol, 26.7% mITT (modified intention-to-treat), not significant.

items.title: Tau-lowering followers: ARO-MAPT (Arrowhead), NIO752 (Novartis), MK-2214 (Merck), VY7523 (Voyager), posdinemab (Johnson & Johnson)
lines: Arrowhead ARO-MAPT under-the-skin siRNA (small interfering RNA) Phase 1: mean tau reduction up to 73% at top dose (October data); possible quarterly dosing.
Novartis NIO752 tau antisense interim analysis presented; figures not reported.
Merck MK-2214 anti-phospho-tau antibody Phase 2 design targets enrollment of 340 early Alzheimer's patients.
J&J symposium dissected failed anti-tau antibody posdinemab; Voyager VY7523 Phase 1/2 baseline characteristics only; figures not reported.

items.title: Brainshuttle AD and PrevenTRON, trontinemab (Roche); real-world donanemab (Eli Lilly)
lines: Updated Phase Ib/IIa data showed rapid amyloid removal and biomarker changes, plus first human imaging of brain distribution; figures not reported.
Roche theory: transferrin-receptor shuttle spares blood-vessel amyloid, possibly explaining low brain-swelling rates; rates not reported in sources reviewed.
PrevenTRON Phase 3 prevention trial in people without symptoms is now enrolling; enrollment target not reported.
Lilly Kisunla real-world data on modified slower dosing from ALZ-NET registry; figures not reported.

expert_minds: Field looking beyond amyloid to tau, oral drugs and psychosis, per BioSpace's preview and the Dementia Researcher wrap-up.
Antibody benefit still debated: Lon Schneider's talk; ARIA meta-analysis of about 5,000 patients found ARIA-E 4.0% vs 12.6% in trial.
Blood biomarkers in almost every session; keynotes by Susan Landau (biomarker integration) and Allan Levey (proteomics).
Combination therapy: Alzheimer's Drug Discovery Foundation called diranersen a natural antibody partner; Roche's Geoffrey Kerchner keynote on prevention.

brief.caveat: Share-price reactions and most p-values or confidence intervals were not found; Acadia, Lilly and AriBio figures come from trade press and a secondary wrap-up, not primary releases.
